paragraphs: Berlin is governed by a coalition of the centre-right CDU (EPP) and the centre-left SPD (S&D) under governing mayor Kai Wegner. It took office after the repeat election of 12 February 2023 — the 26 September 2021 vote had been annulled by the Constitutional Court over ballot shortages, misdelivered papers and hours-long queues, so the outgoing Abgeordnetenhaus sat for three and a half years rather than five. The CDU finished first in that election with 28.2%, its first win in Berlin since 1999.

Polling since has gone the other way on every count. The CDU (EPP) has fallen to around 20%, the SPD (S&D) to 11–15% — which would be its worst Berlin result since reunification — and Die Linke (LEFT) has roughly doubled, from 12.2% in 2023 to between 18% and 23% through 2026, leading or tying the lead in most polls published since July. The AfD (ESN) sits around 18%, the Greens around 16%.

Four parties within a few points of each other is the arithmetic that defines this election: no two-party combination has a clear majority in any recent poll, so 66 of the 130 statutory seats will most likely need three parties. Overhang and levelling seats raise that bar — the chamber has 159 seats at the moment, not 130.

The CDU (EPP) sits with the European People's Party, the SPD (S&D) with the Party of European Socialists, Die Linke (LEFT) with the Party of the European Left, Bündnis 90/Die Grünen with the European Green Party in Greens/EFA, and the FDP (RE) with Renew Europe. The AfD's MEPs sit with the far-right Europe of Sovereign Nations (ESN) group.

Seventeen lists were admitted. The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW (NI)) is contesting Berlin for the first time and has polled at or just below the 5% threshold all year. The FDP (RE) missed the threshold in 2023 with 4.6% and has polled at 3–4% since. Berlin exempts a party that wins a constituency seat outright from the threshold, so a list can enter on district strength alone. Of the non-parliamentary lists in 2023, the Tierschutzpartei came closest with 2.4%; dieBasis contested that election and is not standing again.
